title: Regularization
oneLine: Penalize complexity to trade a little bias for much less variance.

paras: Regularization discourages the model from fitting noise by adding a penalty on the size of its weights. L2 (weight decay) shrinks weights smoothly; L1 drives some to exactly zero, selecting features. Either way you accept slightly more bias for a big drop in variance.
Add a penalty term to the loss, weighted by lambda:
sections.texNote: Larger lambda means simpler models; it is tuned on validation data.

sections.code:
# L2 adds a constant pull toward zero to every gradient step
grad = data_grad(theta) + 2 * lam * theta
theta = theta - eta * grad      # 'weight decay'
sections.caption: A constant shrink toward the origin each update.

takeaways: Regularization penalizes complexity to cut variance.
L2 shrinks smoothly; L1 induces sparsity.
